"My Account: Security and Change Password"

The two self-service Settings tabs every signed-in user has — two-factor authentication, backup codes, recovery email and session sign-out on Security, and the Change Password form.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
📍 WhereSettings → My Account → Security / Change Password (URL /settings/#tab-security, /settings/#tab-password)

What is it?#

My Account is the only Settings group a non-administrator sees, and the page they land on is Security. It holds two tabs: Security (two-factor authentication, recovery email and sign-out) and Change Password. Accounts that sign in through a directory (Active Directory, LDAP or FortiAuthenticator) manage their password and multi-factor authentication at the directory instead.

What does it do?#

  • Two-Factor Authentication (TOTP) — set up an authenticator app, receive ten one-time backup codes, regenerate them, or disable 2FA.
  • Account Recovery — a Recovery email used by Forgot password on the sign-in page.
  • Active Sessions — your current session and a Sign Out button.
  • Change Password — current, new and confirm.

Requirements#

  • A signed-in account. 2FA, backup codes and the recovery email are for local accounts.
  • For password reset by email: server email configured on Email & Alerts and a recovery email on file.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

No permission is needed: every route on these two tabs requires only a signed-in user, and acts only on that user's own account. Directory accounts see "Your account authenticates against a directory — manage multi-factor authentication there." and "Directory accounts recover their password at the directory." instead of the 2FA and recovery controls.

How to use#

Enable two-factor authentication#

  1. Open Settings → My Account → Security and click Set up 2FA.
  2. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app (or type the secret shown).
  3. Enter the 6-digit code under 2. Enter the 6-digit code to confirm: and click Enable.
  4. The flash reads "Two-factor authentication enabled. Save your backup codes now — they are shown only once." Copy the ten codes from the yellow box; they are not shown again.

From then on, sign-in asks for a code after the password; a backup code works once in its place.

Regenerate backup codes#

Click Regenerate backup codes — "New backup codes generated. Save them now — the old ones no longer work." The card always shows Backup codes remaining: N.

Disable two-factor authentication#

Type your password in Confirm password to disable, click Disable 2FA and confirm the dialog Disable two-factor authentication? — "Two-factor authentication disabled."

Set a recovery email#

Enter the address under Recovery email and click Save — "Recovery email updated." Leave it empty and save to remove it ("Recovery email cleared.").

Change your password#

  1. Open Settings → My Account → Change Password.
  2. Fill Current Password, New Password (a strength bar shows Password strength: …) and Confirm New Password.
  3. Click Update Password — "Password changed successfully."

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a new password must have 12 to 1024 characters, the same policy as every other password path (before, this form accepted any non-empty password), and the static Security Status card was removed from the Security tab.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
6-digit code Current TOTP code from the app (one step of clock drift is tolerated). To enable 492817
Confirm password to disable Your current password. To disable —
Recovery email Must contain @ and a dot in the domain; empty clears it. No alice@example.com
Current Password Your current password. Yes —
New Password 12 to 1024 characters, length only (no character-class rule) — the same policy as the profile page, the reset link, the administrator's Add User / Reset password and the root CLI. A shorter password is refused. Yes —
Confirm New Password Must equal the new password. Yes —

Example#

🧪Example — Secure a new local account

After first sign-in, open Security, enable 2FA with your phone, store the ten backup codes in your password manager, set a recovery email, then change the initial password on Change Password.

Result#

  • Audit entries: settings.2fa_enable, settings.2fa_disable, settings.2fa_backup_regen, settings.recovery_email, settings.change_password.
  • The TOTP secret is stored encrypted; backup codes are stored so that each works once.

Troubleshooting#

"Invalid code — 2FA was not enabled. Re-scan the QR and try again."#

Possible causes — wrong code, phone clock out of sync, or the setup was started in another browser tab (the pending secret lives in your session).

Solution — sync the phone's clock, click Set up 2FA again and use the new QR code.

"Password incorrect — 2FA was not disabled."#

Solution — type your current account password.

"Enable two-factor authentication first."#

Solution — backup codes exist only while 2FA is enabled on a local account.

"Directory accounts manage MFA at the directory."#

Solution — use your directory's MFA (for example FortiToken on FortiAuthenticator).

"Current password is incorrect." on Change Password#

Possible causes - A typo in the current password. - Your account is a directory account: it has no usable local password, so this form always fails. Change the password at the directory.

"New passwords do not match." / "A password is required."#

Solution — retype both fields identically.

"The password must be at least 12 characters."#

Possible causes — the new password has fewer than 12 characters.

Solution — choose a password of 12 to 1024 characters. A long passphrase is fine; no particular mix of character types is required.

"Enter a valid email address."#

Solution — correct the recovery email.

"Too many failed attempts — account temporarily locked. Try again later." at sign-in#

Possible causes — ten consecutive failed sign-ins lock the account for 15 minutes.

Solution — wait, or ask an administrator to click Unlock on your row in Users (see Users and profiles).

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • Forgot password sends a reset link valid for one hour, only for active local accounts with a recovery email, and only when server email is configured; the sign-in page never reveals whether the account exists.
  • The link in that email uses the host the request came in on only when it is one of the node's own names or is listed in LINK_HOSTS; any other host is replaced by the node's FQDN. See Configuration files.
  • Active Sessions shows the current session only; signing out elsewhere is not offered.
